citation.title: Pedestal electron collisionality and toroidal rotation during ELM-crash suppression phase under n = 1 RMP in KSTAR
citation.authors: Minwoo Kim, J. Lee, W. H. Ko, S.-H. Hahn, Y. In, Y. M. Jeon, W. Suttrop, S. K. Kim, G. Y. Park, J.-W. Juhn, J. H. Lee

topic: Offline KSTAR pedestal database (n=1 RMP, 28 discharges) relating pedestal collisionality and C6+ CES rotation to ELM-crash suppression versus mitigation.
own_question: Which pedestal-top parameters characterize RMP ELM-crash suppression and separate it from mitigation.
actual_method_and_evidence: Uses Thomson scattering ne/Te and carbon-impurity CES Ti/Vtor, fitted offline with modified tanh profiles to data averaged over about 0.2 s. Applies a collisionality formula with Zeff=2 assumed. Includes MISHKA1 stability analysis, and LDA plus RFE on 7 standardized variables. No nowcasting, causal estimation, BES/ECEI inputs, or held-out validation is reported.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR CES provides carbon-impurity (C6+) Ti and rotation profiles that pedestal studies use offline, e.g., time-averaged and tanh-fitted.
claim_checks.qualification: Impurity Ti, not main-ion Ti. The paper does not discuss CES latency or report timing.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Uses offline averages of about 0.2 s (±0.1 s) around times of interest. CES cadence and arrival times are not stated.
validation_if_relevant: Uses LDA/RFE on a single dataset. No train/test split is described.
forbidden_inferences: That CES Ti is main-ion or physical truth
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include only as optional context: an example of offline use of KSTAR C6+ CES pedestal data. It provides no support for timing, estimation, or validation claims.
